ctx.x: : No, that's really true. Earl Hines is down here.

Father Hines. Let's see. That takes us back to Chicago, the Grand Terrace, where he used to play, aong with Fletcher, you know. There was a guy named Ed Fox that owned the Grand Terrace in Chicago that had Earl Hines under contract, and later on he had Fletcher under contract. And, of course, the original Grand Terrace nightclub first was located at 35th and Giles on the South Side of Chicago; they used to broadcast there, and they had entire revue reviews, with a line of 12 girls, comedians, shows there, like…

And, of course, the Grand Terrace later moved up on 39th and South Park. This is where Count Basie was connected with the Grand Terrace, not the original one. But, nevertheless, getting back to Earl Hines, Earl had some great musicians
